hook_text: The Sahara is almost as big as the United States, and seven hundred years ago people crossed it with no engines at all.
clip_script: Horses die in the Sahara. Oxen die in the Sahara. They need water and grass every single day, and the desert has neither. So how did gold, salt and books cross it for centuries? One animal. The camel. It can walk a week without a drink, then swallow over a hundred litres in minutes. Its hump? Not water: fat, its energy store. Its feet are wide pads that float on sand. Its nostrils snap shut in a sandstorm. Load it with a hundred and fifty kilograms and it walks thirty kilometres a day. Line up a thousand of them, add a guide who reads the stars, and you have a caravan, two months across the desert, carrying the trade that made Mali one of the richest kingdoms on Earth.
visual_style: A whiteboard map of North and West Africa with the Sahara shaded; a fallen horse fades out; a camel walks in, its hump labelled fat, its feet and nostrils highlighted; a long caravan line crosses under a starry sky.
pacing: Strong hook, rapid-fire camel facts, sweeping finish.
